competitive_landscape: Current river traffic is diesel sightseeing boats and slow public ferries; no premium fast zero-emission point-to-point operator exists on the Huangpu. The opportunity is a new premium layer rather than displacing mass transit.
demand_signals: One of the world's densest CBD pairings (Lujiazui finance district and the Bund / Puxi core) separated by the Huangpu — high-value cross-river demand that today relies on bridges, tunnels, metro and slow ferries.
Major waterfront destinations strung along the river: the Bund, Lujiazui, North Bund, West Bund (museum mile), Expo/World Expo Park, and the Shanghai Port International Cruise Terminal.
Strong municipal decarbonization and 'clean Huangpu' policy direction; existing diesel sightseeing fleet is an obvious electrification target.
Large inbound luxury / business-travel base and five-star riverfront hotels (Bund and Lujiazui) that value premium, time-saving arrivals.
Yangtze-estuary leisure and second-home demand toward Chongming Island; longer leg better served by N35 range and speed than by road + bridge.
journeys: A fund manager crosses from a Lujiazui tower to a Bund client dinner in minutes by silent foil instead of a congested tunnel.
A cruise passenger transfers from Wusongkou to a Bund hotel along the river instead of by road.
A family weekends on Chongming Island, reaching an eco-resort by fast estuary shuttle.

navier_fit.charging_note: Riverfront berths at Lujiazui, the Bund and the cruise terminal are natural fast-charge nodes; phased charging spine along the central Huangpu.
navier_fit.draft_note: N35 shallow draft (18") is favorable for creek mouths and tidal estuary berths.
navier_fit.rationale: The Huangpu is a sheltered, deep, year-round navigable urban river ideal for foiling: low wake protects the historic waterfront, silent operation suits a dense CBD, and fast cross-river hops beat congested bridges/tunnels for high-value trips. N30 covers the central cross-river and riverfront circuits; N35 (12-15 pax, shallow draft, 70 nm) handles the longer estuary runs to Chongming and the cruise gateway, and serves resort-style arrivals.

partner_overlays: Hospitality: Bund and Lujiazui five-star riverfront hotels (premium charter + arrivals).
Destination/culture: West Bund museum mile and Expo Park circuits.
Super-app / ridehail adjacency: integration with a domestic mobility platform for booking the premium water leg (China-market platform, e.g. Didi-class operator) — treat as exploratory.
precedents: Navier x JIH Global Maldives ($100M / ~100 vessels / 3-yr) demonstrates large-scale commercial water-mobility deployment.
Four Seasons Lake Austin (N30 live) demonstrates premium hospitality water-arrival operation.
regulatory_note: Huangpu navigation, berthing and commercial water-transport licensing are tightly regulated by Shanghai municipal and port authorities. Any authority engagement must be sequenced and coordinated — not yet initiated. China-market entry would require a domestic partner/operator structure.
seasonality: Year-round navigable; humid subtropical climate. Summer typhoon-season weather windows and winter fog are the main operational considerations; the sheltered river mitigates open-water exposure.

signature_routes.note: core financial-district to historic waterfront link

sources: Public geography of the Huangpu River, Suzhou Creek, and Yangtze estuary
Public knowledge of Shanghai waterfront destinations (Bund, Lujiazui, West Bund, Expo Park, cruise terminal)
General municipal decarbonization / clean-waterway policy direction
summary: Shanghai is built around water: the Huangpu River bisects the city between the Bund and Lujiazui, the Suzhou Creek threads the historic core, and the Yangtze estuary opens to Chongming Island and the East China Sea. Today the river carries heavy commercial traffic plus diesel sightseeing and commuter ferries; there is no premium, fast, zero-emission point-to-point water layer linking the financial districts, riverfront destinations, and the cruise/airport gateways. Navier's hydrofoiling N30/N35 fit the sheltered Huangpu corridor and the longer estuary runs, offering a quiet, wake-light, fast alternative that complements the metro for high-value cross-river and riverfront journeys.
tagline: The Huangpu spine — a global financial waterfront ready for a silent, fast water layer.

transit_planning.authority_note: Shanghai municipal transport and port authorities govern Huangpu navigation; commercial waterfront berths are tightly managed. Treat any authority engagement as sequenced and coordinated — not yet initiated.
transit_planning.complements: Metro Lines crossing the Huangpu, cross-river bus/tunnel, and the existing public ferry; Navier adds a premium fast layer, not a mass-transit replacement.

use_cases: Premium cross-river shuttle: Lujiazui (financial district) <-> the Bund / North Bund, minutes door-to-door, silent and wake-light.
Riverfront destination hopper: West Bund museum mile <-> Expo Park <-> the Bund for culture/leisure circuits.
Cruise-terminal & gateway transfer: Shanghai Port International Cruise Terminal / Wusongkou <-> central riverfront hotels.
Estuary leisure run: central Shanghai <-> Chongming Island eco-resorts (longer N35 leg).
Corporate / hospitality charter for the dense Lujiazui + Bund five-star hotel cluster.
